title: The LLC Resonant Converter
subject: Power Electronics
blurb: Why half-bridge LLC exists, what the tank actually does, and how to read the gain curve without guessing.
prerequisites: AC circuit analysis in phasor form

slides.title:
The LLC Resonant
Converter
slides.lead: Why the topology exists, what the tank is really doing, and how to read the gain curve without guessing.

slides.title:
You cannot shrink the magnetics
without cooking the FETs
slides.lead: Every designer gets the same instruction: make it smaller. Smaller means higher switching frequency, because magnetic volume falls as frequency rises. That part works. What happens to the switches does not.

columns.label: And you pay for it
items: Switching loss scales directly with frequency
Every turn-on dumps the energy stored in C<sub>oss</sub>
V and I overlap during the transition, heating the die
EMI gets worse at exactly the frequencies that matter

slides.callout: In a hard-switched converter, switching loss is roughly proportional to frequency. Double the frequency, double the loss. That is the wall — and resonant conversion is the attempt to walk through it.

slides.title:
Turn the switch on when its voltage
is already zero

points.text: Loss comes from overlap. If Vds has already fallen to zero before the gate rises, there is no overlap and no turn-on loss.
The tank must be inductive. Current has to lag the voltage so it keeps flowing after turn-off and discharges Coss.
The dead time has to be long enough. Drop the current or shorten the dead time and the discharge never finishes.

slides.callout: Drag the sliders. Whatever voltage is left on C<sub>oss</sub> at turn-on gets dissipated inside the die — this is how FETs die in a badly tuned resonant converter.

slides.title:
Half-bridge, three reactive elements,
transformer, rectifier

legend.role: Half-bridge at fixed 50% duty with dead time. Regulation comes from frequency, never duty.
Resonant capacitor. Also blocks DC, so the transformer never sees a DC bias.
Resonant inductor. Often just transformer leakage — which is why construction matters so much.
Magnetizing inductance, deliberately made small enough to take part in resonance.
Isolation and the turns ratio n that sets the nominal operating point.
Rectifier. Reflects the load back into the tank as an equivalent AC resistance.

slides.callout: Three reactive elements — two inductors and one capacitor — is where the name comes from: L, L, C.

slides.title: There are two resonant frequencies
slides.lead: Most explanations quote a single resonant frequency and then cannot explain the shape of the gain curve. The circuit has two, and the entire operating map lives between them.

formulas.label: Series resonance
formulas.note: Lm is shorted by the reflected load, so only Lr and Cr resonate. Here the tank is purely resistive and gain is 1 at any load. This is the design anchor.

formulas.label: Magnetizing resonance
formulas.note: When the secondary stops conducting, Lm is unclamped and joins the resonance. Because Lm is much larger than Lr, this sits well below fr.

points.text: Above fr the converter behaves like a series resonant circuit — gain is always below 1.
Between fm and fr the converter can boost above 1. This is the useful region.
Below fm the tank turns capacitive, ZVS is lost, and the design fails.
